data: This course offers an introduction to the fundamental concepts in the psychology oflanguage, exploring the nature of Natural Language and how it is structured andprocessed by the human brain. Students will delve into key topics such as syntax, orsentence structure, and phonology, the sound structure of language. The course alsoexamines the cognitive processes underlying language comprehension and production,and how natural language is represented and processed in the brain. The course willintroduce to formal theories of Language, focusing on Syntax, Phonology andPhonetics, and subsequently guide them through psycholinguistic theories of linguisticprocessing in the brain. Besides being introduced to the theoretical and experimentalconcepts foundational to the field, the students are also exposed to the history of thedevelopment of psycholinguistic thought, and the various frameworks of psychology thatare relevant to understanding Natural Languages. Through a combination of lectures,discussions, and hands-on laboratory activities, students will gain a deeperunderstanding of the complex relationship between language and the mind.
